title: Fun at Kids Central

subtitle.text: Nina watched the other second graders run outside.
Their parents were picking them up.
But Nina's mom worked late.
So Nina was going to Kids Central.
Nina walked into the gym.
She wished she could go home and play in her backyard.
A big banner over the windows read "After-School Fun & Games @ Kids Central!"
[g@Nina didn't see anyone she knew.
She felt nervous.@g]
"Oh, there's my name."
Nina spotted a name tag with her name on it and sat down.
Izzie was excited to be at Kids Central.
But her name tag was wrong.
"Isabel?" Izzie read. "I'm Izzie, not Isabel!"
Izzie looked at the boy next to her.
"You must be Jason."
"Welcome, everyone! Please find your seat," Miss Shelly called.
Miss Shelly was the Kids Central teacher.
Nina thought she had a nice smile.
"Today we're going to decorate name tags," Miss Shelly said.
[g@A tall boy sat down next to Nina.
He didn't say hello.@g]
But his name tag said "BOBBY."
"Look through the magazines on your table.
Cut out pictures of things you like," Miss Shelly said.
"For example, Nina, what do you like?" Miss Shelly asked.
Nina smiled.
"I like the color purple and I like my rain boots," she answered shyly.
[g@"Nice! Jason, what do you like?"
Miss Shelly waited. "Jason?"@g]
[g@Izzie poked Jason's arm.
"He likes video games," she said.@g]
"Jason, we don't play video games at Kids Central.
Please put that away." Miss Shelly sounded serious.
"Besides video games, what do you like?"
Jason looked up. "Cheeseburgers."
"Great! Start cutting!" Miss Shelly pointed to the magazines.
"Please pass me that magazine," Nina said.
"Please pass me those scissors," Bobby said.
Izzie waved her hand in the air.
"Miss Shelly? I need a new name tag.
[g@Only my grandma calls me Isabel.
Everyone calls me Izzie."@g]
"I'm sorry! You can make a new name tag."
Miss Shelly handed her some stiff paper.
"Punch two holes in the top." Izzie punched.
"Then write your name in big, beautiful letters.
[g@Now take all the pictures you cut out.
Glue them onto your name tag.@g]
You can glue them on the front, on the back, or on both sides!
When you're done, choose a piece of yarn.
Thread it through the holes on your tag.
Ta-da! Your name tag becomes a necklace!"
Miss Shelly tied her name tag around her neck.
"You could also hang it on your bedroom doorknob."
"Nina, your mom's here," Miss Shelly called.
Nina looked surprised. "Is Kids Central over already?"
"Yep. Time to go home, sweetie," her mom said.
[g@"Bye, Miss Shelly!" Nina ran to her mom.
"Look what I made!"@g]
[caption_out@
[g@Bobby walked into the gym after school.
It was raining.@g]
So Kids Central was inside today.
He wished they could go outside and play.
[g@He also wished he had brought a snack.
He was hungry.@g]
"You guys look tired today.
Maybe we need a snack to wake everyone up," Miss Shelly said.
"Yeah!" Bobby agreed.
"My mom makes coffee when she's tired," Nina said.
[g@Miss Shelly laughed.
"We're going to make something better than coffee.@g]
We're going to make our very own Kids Central energy bars.
Everyone, gather around this big bowl."
"Cool. We're making our own snack!" Bobby said.
[g@"We'll make the mixture all together.
The instructions are on the board."@g]
"Step 1: Empty one can of condensed milk and two tablespoons of oil into a bowl. Stir," Miss Shelly read.
Nina picked up an open can on the table.
"Here is the condensed milk."
"I've got the oil."
Jason measured two tablespoons of oil and poured them into the bowl. "Stir!"
"Step 2: Add two cups of toasted oats. Stir."
Nina picked up a bag of toasted oats.
"How much is two cups?"
[g@Bobby handed her a measuring cup.
"Fill this up twice."@g]
"One. Two. There!" Nina grinned. "This is fun."
"Step 3: Add one cup of puffed wheat. Stir."
Jason measured one cup and added it to the mixing bowl.
"Cool. That was easy."
"Step 4: Add half a cup of chopped nuts.
Where are the chopped nuts, Miss Shelly?" Izzie asked.
[g@"Here are the chopped nuts.
We're using sliced almonds."@g]
Miss Shelly handed her the bag of nuts.
Izzie added them to the mix.
[g@"Step 5: Make it sweet.
Add chocolate chips and raisins," Nina read.@g]
"Ooh, I love raisins."
[g@"Don't forget step 6: Add one cup of sunflower seeds,"
Miss Shelly reminded them.@g]
"And don't forget to stir, stir, stir!" Izzie said.
"I am stirring, stirring, stirring," Nina said.
"Spread onto a greased baking pan.
How do you grease the pan, Miss Shelly?" Bobby asked.
"Pour some oil onto a paper towel," she answered.
"Then rub it around the bottom of the pan.
Miss Shelly gave him a paper towel.
"Now we press the mixture down like this."
Miss Shelly pressed her palms firmly on top of the mixture.
"We're ready to bake!"
Miss Shelly lifted the pan into the toaster oven.
"Bake for 25 minutes at 175 degrees Celsius," Bobby said.
"What will we do for 25 minutes?" Jason asked.
[g@"Let's play soccer.
Girls versus boys!" Bobby shouted.@g]
"Yeah! Boys win!" Jason and Bobby slapped hands.
"Mmm . . . Something smells good!" Bobby cried.
"It's our snack!" Miss Shelly said.
"It's ready for the final step."
"Cut into bars and enjoy," Bobby read.
[g@"That means eat!
Maybe staying inside isn't so bad after all."@g]
[g@Miss Shelly cut 12 bars.
Everyone took an energy bar.@g]
"Wow. We made a really good snack!" Izzie said.
"Yeah. And now I have lots of energy," added Bobby.
"Let's go play more soccer!"
[caption_out@
Jason was swimming away from a great white shark when someone tapped him on the shoulder.
"Jason," Miss Shelly said.
"I've warned you about video games in Kids Central . . ."
"Sorry, Miss Shelly," Jason mumbled.
He looked down and saw himself get eaten by the shark.
"Did everyone bring in a plastic garbage bag and a newspaper?" Miss Shelly asked the kids.
"Yes. But what are they for?" Nina wanted to know.
"It's a surprise," Miss Shelly said, her eyes twinkling.
"Everyone, grab two paint pens and a ruler from the table.
Toss them in your bags and follow me outside!"
Miss Shelly led the class to the picnic tables on the playground.
"We're lucky we have these tables.
But what if we wanted to sit under that tree over there?
Or in a park that doesn't have tables?"
The kids stared at her.
"The ground is all wet," Miss Shelly hinted.
"[i@We'd@i] get all wet," Bobby said.
"We'd need something to sit on!" Izzie burst out.
"Yes! We'd need something like a sit-upon!" Miss Shelly said.
"Today we're going to make sit-upons.
Take everything out of your bag except for the newspaper.
First we have to cut your garbage bags to make them smaller.
Let your newspaper slide all the way to the bottom of the bag.
Measure about ten centimeters from the end of the newspaper.
Then cut off the open end of the bag."
Miss Shelly handed out scissors.
"Measure," Bobby said, placing a ruler on his bag.
"Cut," Nina said, cutting her bag.
"Perfect!" Izzie said, holding up her bag.
"Now fold the loose side, like you're wrapping a present.
Then tape the end with duct tape.
Be careful. Duct tape is very sticky!"
Jason sat with his arms crossed, looking unhappy.
"What's the matter, Jason?" Miss Shelly asked.
"I don't like this craft," he said grumpily.
"Why not?" Miss Shelly frowned.
[g@"My mom gave me a pink garbage bag!
I hate pink!"@g]
Jason pushed his bag away from him.
"Oh, Jason. Pink is a great color.
But if you want a different bag . . . Let's see . . .
Does anyone want to trade bags with Jason?"
"I do!" Izzie jumped up. "I love pink!"
[g@"Thank you, Izzie.
What color is your bag?" Miss Shelly asked.@g]
"Gray. Is that okay?" Izzie looked at Jason.
"Gray is my favorite color." Jason grinned.
"Problem solved. Now everyone is going to paint their sit-upons!"
Miss Shelly turned to the other kids.
"Use your paint pens to decorate your sit-upon any way you'd like!
Make sure to put your name on it.
Then you're all done!"
"Wow, Jason. That's cool," Izzie said.
Jason had drawn a great white shark on his sit-upon.
"Thanks. I guess it's okay.
But it would have looked dumb on a pink bag!" he said.
[caption_out@
Izzie and Nina were swinging high on the swings.
They had just met at Kids Central a few weeks ago.
But Izzie liked Nina.
"Fall is my favorite season," Izzie said.
"Yeah. I love fall too," Nina agreed.
"Girls! Come get your sit-upons.
You'll need them soon!" Miss Shelly called.
It was time for the Kids Central activity of the day.
"I wonder what we're doing," Izzie said.
[g@Miss Shelly was holding a brown paper bag.
She wore tall rubber boots.@g]
"Out to the woods we go!" she said.
[g@Everyone followed Miss Shelly onto a path.
The path went into the woods.@g]
[g@"Here we are," Miss Shelly said.
"Our campground for the day."@g]
"What are we doing here?" Izzie asked.
"Can we put our sit-upons anywhere?" Bobby asked.
"Anywhere that looks comfortable to sit," Miss Shelly answered.
Miss Shelly emptied her shopping bag onto the ground.
"For today's activity we'll use a fire, marshmallows, chocolate, and graham crackers.
Can anyone guess what it is?"
"S'mores!" Bobby yelled. "My favorite!"
"Yum! My family makes s'mores when we go camping," Nina said.
"What's a s'more?" Izzie asked.
"What's a [i@s'more@i]?" Nina repeated, shocked.
"You're in for a treat today, Izzie." Miss Shelly smiled.
"First I'll make the fire.
[g@You should each find a long, skinny stick.
Brush off any dirt.@g]
You can peel off the bark, if you'd like," Miss Shelly instructed.
[g@"Oh, I found a perfect one!"
Nina said, brushing off a long stick.@g]
"We use these to roast the marshmallows," Jason told Izzie.
"Yep. You put the marshmallow on the end of your stick. Like this."
Bobby showed Izzie how to stab the marshmallow.
[g@Izzie held up her stick.
"Okay, now what?"@g]
"Now let's roast these marshmallows!" Miss Shelly said.
"Hold your stick carefully [i@over@i] the fire, but not [i@in@i] the fire."
[g@"I like mine gooey and dripping.
That's the best," Nina said.@g]
"No way. Totally burnt and crispy on the outside is the best," Bobby said.
[g@Izzie screamed.
"Miss Shelly! My marshmallow is on fire!"@g]
[g@"Don't worry, Izzie.
Just blow it out, like a birthday candle."@g]
Miss Shelly calmly took Izzie's stick and blew out the small flame.
[g@"So this is a s'more?"
Izzie asked, holding up her burnt marshmallow.@g]
"Not yet. Now we take two graham crackers," Nina said.
"And a piece of chocolate," Jason added.
"Put your chocolate on one graham cracker.
[g@And put your marshmallow on top of the chocolate."
Bobby showed her how.@g]
"Then put your other graham cracker on top, like a sandwich.
[g@And squish it together."
Nina squished her sandwich.@g]
[g@Melted chocolate dripped out of one side.
Izzie and Nina laughed.@g]
[g@"S'mores are so good!"
Izzie wiped marshmallow off her lips.@g]
"Aren't they? They're perfect for a fall day." Miss Shelly smiled.
Izzie looked around at the pretty fall leaves.
Then she looked at her new friend Nina.
[g@Miss Shelly was right.
Everything was perfectly perfect.@g]
[caption_out@

episodes.title: A Fair Game of Four Square

subtitle.text: Bobby was dribbling a basketball on the blacktop.
He was pretending to be on the Eagles, the high school's team.
Miss Shelly was getting ready to start an activity.
"It'd better be fun," Bobby thought.
He didn't want to stop playing basketball.
Miss Shelly had a big box of chalk and a ball.
[g@She blew her whistle.
"Let's gather on the blacktop!" she called.@g]
"I want to be on Izzie's team!" Nina cried.
"You don't even know what we're doing yet," Bobby said.
[g@"We're going to play a game.
It's called Four Square," Miss Shelly said.@g]
[g@Bobby knew Four Square.
His sisters played it.@g]
Kids Central was going to be fun today.
"Who has played Four Square before?" Miss Shelly asked.
[g@Only Bobby raised his hand.
"I'm going to be the best!" he thought.@g]
"Bobby, would you draw a Four Square board for us?" Miss Shelly asked.
She held out the chalk.
Bobby drew a large square and then divided it into four smaller squares.
He numbered them 1, 2, 3, 4.
"I start by passing the ball to Bobby," explained Miss Shelly.
"The ball must bounce [i@once@i] in my square and then go into Bobby's.
If the ball lands on any line, I am out.
Bobby must hit the ball with his hands and bounce the ball to another square.
If he doesn't, he is out.
If the ball goes out of the big square without bouncing in any square, he is out.
If he catches the ball, he is out.
If Bobby is out, he will go to square 1.
The person in square 1 will move to square 2, and so on.
We will play for five minutes.
Whoever is in square 4 at the end wins!
Bobby, you're in square 1. Izzie, square 2. Jason, 3. Nina, 4."
[g@"That's not fair!" Bobby cried.
"I'm going to lose!"@g]
"It's ABC order, Bobby," Miss Shelly replied.
[g@"Square 4 starts.
Here you go, Nina!"@g]
"Ready?" Nina said. Everyone nodded.
She bounced the ball to Jason in square 3.
[g@Jason bounced the ball to Izzie.
Izzie bounced the ball to Bobby.@g]
[g@Bobby bounced the ball back to Izzie.
But she missed!@g]
"You're out!" Bobby shouted.
"Bobby, there's no need to yell," Miss Shelly warned.
"Nina, go ahead and start again."
Nina bounced the ball to Jason.
"Ten seconds left," Miss Shelly called.
Bobby panicked. He had to get Nina out to win.
But no one was passing him the ball!
"Three, two, one. Game over," Miss Shelly said.
"No!" Bobby groaned.
[g@"Hooray, I win!" Nina cried.
"Four Square is fun."@g]
"Yay, Nina," Izzie cheered.
"Four Square is no fair," Bobby said, frowning.
"Four Square is good practice for basketball, isn't it?" Miss Shelly said.
[g@Bobby paused.
"Yeah, I guess so.
It's good practice for passing.@g]
Hey, Miss Shelly, when can we play again?"
[caption_out@
Nina took her apron out of her backpack.
Miss Shelly had asked all the Kids Central kids to bring aprons today.
[g@Nina's apron was purple.
It was a present from Aunt Sujong in Korea.@g]
Aunt Sujong visited the United States once a year.
"Hey, Bobby. Nice apron," Jason teased.
Bobby was wearing a pink apron with ruffles.
[g@"It's my sister's," Bobby grumbled.
"What are you wearing?"@g]
[g@"My old pajamas," Jason said.
"It's also my smock for art class."@g]
[g@"[i@Buon giorno@i]!" Miss Shelly called.
She was wearing a chef's hat.@g]
"That's Italian for 'hello.'
Today we're going to make my favorite Italian food—pizza!
But we're going to make small snack pizzas called pizza bagels!"
[g@"I've eaten bagels.
And I've eaten pizza.@g]
But I've never eaten [i@pizza bagels@i] before!" Nina said.
"First you can each take six bagel halves from the basket," Miss Shelly told them.
"Whoa! We each get six?" Bobby cried.
"Yep. What's next, Bobby?" Miss Shelly asked.
"Spread pizza sauce on the bagels," Bobby read.
Nina spread the sauce in a circle on her bagels.
[g@"Wait, I need more."
Jason leaned over the table to take the jar from Nina.@g]
His bagels slipped off his dish.
"Ah!" Nina jumped out of the way of the sliding bagels.
[i@Splat@i]. Jason's bagels landed sauce-side down on the gym floor.
"Oh!" Jason moaned. "Now what, Miss Shelly?"
"Sorry. We only had enough for six each.
Someone will have to share with you," Miss Shelly answered.
"I'll share mine," Bobby said.
"Thank you, Bobby," said Miss Shelly. "That's very kind."
[g@"Now sprinkle shredded cheese on the bagels.
Not too much," Nina read out loud.@g]
"Yum, I love cheese!" Izzie cried.
[g@"Then choose a topping.
Sprinkle it over the cheese," Izzie read.@g]
"I pick bacon."
"I pick olives," Nina said.
[g@"Look! I'm making a pizza pie!"
The girls turned around.@g]
Bobby was tossing two bagels in the air.
[g@He was pretending to make pizza dough.
Jason was laughing.@g]
"Boys, do not play with food," Miss Shelly warned.
"Whoa!" Bobby tripped and bumped into Jason.
Their plate went flying into the air.
[g@Jason leaped to catch it.
But it was too late.@g]
"Six more pizza bagels gone." Miss Shelly sighed.
"Well, let's put yours in the toaster oven, girls."
"Something is burning!" Miss Shelly ran to the toaster oven.
"My pizza bagels!" Izzie cried.
"Too much cheese," Jason said.
The cheese had dripped off the bagels.
It was burned onto the bottom of the oven.
[g@"But there are still six good pizza bagels here."
Miss Shelly pulled Nina's bagels out of the oven.@g]
[g@"Enough for all of us." Nina smiled.
"Dig in, everyone."@g]
"Thanks. Hooray for Nina!" everyone cheered.
Miss Shelly took off her chef's hat and put it on Nina's head.
Nina beamed. She couldn't wait to make pizza bagels for Aunt Sujong.
[caption_out@
[g@"Hi, Miss Shelly.
What are we doing today?"@g]
Jason was the first to arrive in the gym for Kids Central.
"Hello, Jason. I can't tell you until everyone else arrives.
But you can help me pass out these index cards," Miss Shelly said.
[g@"Hi." Nina walked in next.
"What are the cards for?"@g]
"We can't find out until everyone gets here," Jason told her.
Bobby and Izzie walked in.
[g@"Let's start!" Jason told Miss Shelly.
"Everyone is here."@g]
"Jason, let me sit down first. Geesh!"
Izzie rolled her eyes at Nina and sat down at the table.
"Okay, [i@now@i] I'm ready."
"Today we will do something impossible," Miss Shelly said.
"No way. That's impossible!" Bobby said. Everyone laughed.
"Hold up your index card.
Which is bigger, the card or your face?" Miss Shelly asked.
"My face," Izzie and Nina said at the same time.
"Of course my face," Bobby said.
[g@But Jason shook his head.
He had seen magic shows before.@g]
"Is this a trick question?" he asked.
"I think the card is bigger."
"You think the card is bigger?
[g@Let's measure and see," Miss Shelly said.
"How big is the card?"@g]
Bobby measured. "13 centimeters wide and 8 centimeters tall."
"Have you ever measured your face?" Miss Shelly asked.
"My face is 17 centimeters long and 12 centimeters wide," Jason said.
"So your head is bigger.
[g@But I bet you can fit your head through this little index card."
Miss Shelly held up her card.@g]
"What? No way!" Jason said.
"Impossible," Bobby said.
"I bet Miss Shelly can do it," Izzie said.
She smiled at her favorite teacher.
"Well, I'll show you a trick," Miss Shelly said.
"A magic trick?" Jason asked.
[g@"Not a magic trick.
A real trick," she answered.@g]
"Step 1: Fold your card in half from top to bottom.
Step 2: Make 13 small cuts on the folded side of your card."
Everyone cut carefully.
"Step 3: Make 13 small cuts on the open side of your card.
Step 4: Carefully unfold your card and cut along the fold.
But do not cut the first edge or the last edge.
What do you have?"
[g@Jason unfolded his card.
His eyes opened wide.@g]
[g@"Wow! It's huge.
And my head fits through it!"@g]
"But it's still just a regular index card."
Miss Shelly put her card back together.
"That's a cool trick, Miss Shelly," Jason said.
"Will you teach us more like that?"
"Sure. But right now I think your dad's waiting for you."
She pointed to the door.
"Dad!" Jason jumped up.
"Want to see a cool trick?
I can put my head through an index card!"
[caption_out@
[g@Izzie looked out the window.
It looked cold and gray outside.@g]
[g@But there was no snow.
Christmas was only two weeks away.@g]
Izzie hoped it would be a white Christmas.
She closed her eyes and wished for snow.
"Hey, Izzie," Nina said.
She pointed to a pile of paper plates and paints on the table.
"I think we're doing a craft."
"Oh good," said Izzie.
[g@She loved crafts.
And Miss Shelly always had fun ideas.@g]
"Today we are going to make holiday wreaths."
Miss Shelly held up a glittering gold and silver wreath.
[g@"Ooh, it's pretty," Izzie said.
"I like the angel."@g]
"Me too," Nina said.
"Is that a paper plate?" Jason asked.
"It is. We're going to make wreaths out of paper plates, paint, glue, and some other things."
Miss Shelly held up a bag.
"I have a bunch of old holiday decorations.
You can use whatever you want.
First fold your paper plate in half.
And then cut a half circle out of the middle," Miss Shelly said.
[g@"It looks like a wreath already,"
Izzie said, unfolding her plate.@g]
"Now paint your wreath and decorate it with anything you want."
Miss Shelly pointed to a pile of decorations on the table.
[g@"I'll use this."
Bobby held up a paper bell.@g]
[g@"And I'll use this."
Jason held up a paper menorah.@g]
"Oh!" Nina and Izzie spotted the angel at the same time.
"It's mine!" They both reached for the angel.
"Nina, I [i@really@i] want it," Izzie said.
"So do I, Izzie," Nina said.
"Girls, is there a problem?" Miss Shelly asked.
"Nina wants to use my angel," Izzie said.
"[i@Your@i] angel?" Nina raised her eyebrows.
[g@"Should we share it?"
Nina asked, looking at Miss Shelly.@g]
"You two girls are smart.
I'm sure you'll figure something out," Miss Shelly said.
[g@"Share it?" Izzie repeated.
"How do you share an angel?"@g]
"I guess we could cut it in half," Nina said.
[g@Izzie felt like crying.
She didn't want half of the angel.@g]
Half of the angel would not be beautiful.
She wanted the whole angel.
[g@"It's okay," Izzie said quietly.
"Nina can have it."@g]
She looked away as Nina took the ornament.
[g@"Thank you, Izzie," Miss Shelly said.
"That was very grown-up."@g]
[g@Izzie saw Nina's wreath drying on the floor.
It looked good.@g]
"Please make it snow," Izzie whispered to the angel.
While their wreaths were drying, Miss Shelly brought out a bucket of jingle bells.
They sang holiday songs and shook their bells.
Before Izzie knew it, it was time to go home.
"What a cute wreath, Izzie!" Izzie's mom exclaimed.
She and Nina's mom were holding up the wreaths.
"Izzie, come look!" Nina suddenly shouted.
[g@Izzie ran to the window.
She couldn't believe it.@g]
[g@It was snowing!
Her wish had come true.@g]
She looked at Nina's wreath and silently thanked the angel.
[g@Then she turned to Nina.
"Come on, let's catch snowflakes!"@g]
[caption_out@
Bobby opened the door to the gym.
Jason, Nina, and Izzie were there already, ready for Kids Central.
Miss Shelly was passing out sweatbands.
"What are we doing today, Miss Shelly?" Bobby asked.
"We are exercising," Miss Shelly answered.
"Are we playing basketball?" Bobby asked excitedly.
"We're doing a different kind of exercise," she said.
"Today we'll exercise our brains!"
The kids looked at each other.
"Our brains? Does that mean we're doing math?" Nina asked, frowning.
Bobby groaned.
"Not quite. I have a bucket here full of brain teasers."
Miss Shelly held up a bucket of cards.
"Here, Nina," Miss Shelly said.
"Pick a card and read the brain teaser to yourself.
Then choose someone to answer it."
[g@Nina took a card and read it silently.
Then she grinned.@g]
"I choose Bobby," she said.
"How many letters are in the alphabet?" Nina asked.
"That's easy. 26," Bobby answered.
Nina burst into giggles.
[g@"Nope. 11! [i@T-h-e-a-l-p-h-a-b-e-t.@i]
Get it? That's 11!"@g]
[g@She smiled at Miss Shelly.
"This is fun."@g]
[g@"Okay, Bobby, you're next.
Pick a card," Miss Shelly said.@g]
Bobby took a card and read it.
"Jason!" he said, turning to his friend.
"What goes up but never comes down?"
Jason shrugged. "A hot air balloon? Clouds?"
"You can only have one answer!" Bobby said.
"Okay, clouds."
"Nope. Your age!" Bobby waved the card in front of Jason.
"My turn," Jason said, taking a card out of the bucket.
"Aha! This is a good one." He turned to Izzie.
"What doesn't get any wetter, even in the rain?"
[g@Izzie thought for a moment.
"An umbrella?" she guessed.@g]
"No. Water!" Jason said happily.
"Okay. Here I go.
Nina, what is full of holes but still holds water?" Izzie asked.
"[i@There's a hole in the bucket . . . @i]," Nina began to sing softly.
"A basket!" she cried.
[g@"No, but good try!
The answer is a sponge," Izzie told her friend.@g]
"Miss Shelly, now it's your turn!" Jason said.
[g@"Okay. Here I go."
Miss Shelly took a card, closed her eyes, and spun around in a circle.@g]
When she stopped, she was facing Bobby.
"Bobby," Miss Shelly said.
[g@"The more of them you take, the more you leave behind.
What are they?"@g]
Bobby thought.
"The more of them you take, the more you leave behind," he repeated to himself.
"I take showers . . . I take naps . . . I take steps . . . Steps! Footsteps!
That's the answer, Miss Shelly," Bobby said.
Miss Shelly clapped her hands and laughed.
"Well done!" she said. "You got it."
"These were hard brain teasers," Nina said. "My head hurts!"
"Miss Shelly, can I take home the brain-teaser bucket?" Bobby asked.
"I'm going to learn every brain teaser in the world!"
[caption_out@
[g@Nina glanced down the hallway.
It was empty.@g]
She quickly pulled her jump rope out of her backpack.
Then she began to skip down the hall.
[g@"Hey. Stop it right there.
No jumping inside!" someone called.@g]
Nina froze. She turned around and saw the fifth-grade hall monitor.
Where had he come from?

episodes.title: Friendship Bracelets for Girls and Boys

subtitle.text: Izzie saw Ethan in the hallway ahead of her.

"I think they're goofy."
[g@"They are [i@not@i] goofy," Mr. Dunn said.
"They're part of a meaningful tradition."@g]
He looked at Bobby.
"When a friend gives you a bracelet, you should never cut it off.
You wear it for as long as the two of you remain friends."
"I can't wait to make mine!" said Izzie.
"First choose three colors," Mr. Dunn instructed.
[g@"This is pretty."
Izzie reached for a bundle of blue thread.@g]
But her hand bumped into another hand reaching for the same one.
"Sorry," Ethan mumbled. "I'll pick a different one."
"You can choose the same color," Mr. Dunn said.
"Izzie, measure out sixty centimeters, and then give Ethan the thread."
Everyone measured and cut six strands of thread.
Then Mr. Dunn showed them what to do.
"Now tie a knot ten centimeters from one end.
[g@Next tape that end to the table.
After that separate the strands by color.@g]
There should be two strands of each color."
"Now we're ready to weave!" said Nina.
Mr. Dunn nodded. "Start with the strand all the way to the left.
Use it to tie a knot around the string next to it.
Keep going all the way across.
Once you've knotted each string, start again on the left.
Do you understand?" Mr. Dunn asked.
[g@"Yep!" Izzie said.
This looked like it would take a while.@g]
She wanted to finish hers today.
"Weave away! Ask me if you need help," said Mr. Dunn.
"I'm making mine for you," Nina whispered to Izzie.

"Thanks." Then she got back to work.

Izzie's hands were cramping and her neck hurt from bending over.
But her bracelet looked great.
"Okay, campers. Time to get out into that sunshine and play some kickball," Mr. Dunn said.
"If you're not done with your bracelets, you can finish them at home," Mr. Dunn added.
